summary: Throughput collapse on dedicated cluster caused by telemetry sidecar burst + NVLink saturations blocking autoscaler signals
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Qrious observed a sharp throughput collapse (p50 throughput ~60% of baseline, p99 token latency up to 3x) on their dedicated reserved pool in us-west-2 between 2026-03-12 09:15 and 11:50 UTC. The path to error shows autoscaler failing to provision additional GPU slots despite elevated queue depth. Primary symptoms point to an adjacent telemetry sidecar from a customer analytics adapter emitting large batched samples that coincided with a prefetch warmup, which overloaded NVLink/PCIe fabric on several nodes and caused blocked kernel IO and attach delays.

Impact:
- Customer-facing LLM requests experienced increased latencies and a 25-40% drop in successful throughput for 2+ hours.
- Failing live canary and A/B rollout for Qrious; product team escalated to support.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Deploy a reserved pool replication in a staging cluster configured to mirror customer's burst pattern (small long-lived streams + sidecar telemetry bursts every 30s).
2) Start load generator (short multi-turn chat streams at 8 rps per tenant) while enabling sidecar telemetry flood at 200MB/s sustained for 60s bursts.
3) Observe queue depth growth, delayed GPU attach logs and autoscaler failing to register capacity changes for 45-90s.

Observed logs/metrics (selected excerpts):
- serving-runtime: "attach_request=queued duration_ms=7450 reason=nvlink_io_wait"
- autoscaler: "telemetry-lag=120s; decision=hold; reason=missing-utilization-samples"
- kernel/dmesg (node-7): "nvlink: peer stall detected, retrying"
- metrics: p99_token_latency increased from 220ms -> 720ms, avg_gpu_util unchanged (~40%) but io_wait spike + NVLink error counters increased 20x.

Customer notes: Qrious runs a lightweight analytics sidecar that recently rolled a telemetry change (v2.3.4) increasing batch size and switching to persistent NVMe-backed buffers. They rolled this at 2026-03-12 08:50 UTC; problem onset closely follows.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:05 - Triage by Support (Sofia): Confirmed customer impact, raised P1. Collected relevant telemetry URLs and requested dedicated logs from node pool.

2026-03-12 11:00 - SRE (Ethan): Reproduced high attach latencies in staging when replaying telemetry burst. Observed autoscaler metrics lag — aggregator drop rate increased during burst leading to stale utilization windows.
2026-03-12 11:20 - SRE: kernel logs on three nodes show repeated NVLink stall warnings and a pattern of increased pci_io_wait which correlates with sidecar flush windows (every 30s).

2026-03-12 11:45 - Support: Notified customer with temporary mitigation steps (throttle sidecar, reduce batch size to 1MB, stagger flushes). Customer applied throttle and reported partial recovery within 6 minutes.

2026-03-12 12:10 - Eng: Performed manual scale-up (allocated two extra GPU slots) to relieve queue while autoscaler telemetry pipeline recovered. Throughput returned ~85% of baseline after scale-up + sidecar throttle.

2026-03-12 14:00 - Eng: Identified autoscaler dependency on single telemetry aggregator path; when aggregator's ingress backpressures, utilization samples drop below threshold and autoscaler holds instead of scaling.
2026-03-13 09:00 - Patch created: implement rate-limiter in sidecar ingestion path and add backpressure metrics to autoscaler decisions (PR linked).
2026-03-14 08:30 - Monitoring: Added NVLink error counters to dedicated pool alerting to detect fabric saturation earlier.
resolution_notes: Temporary workaround: Customer throttled telemetry sidecar to <10MB/s burst and staggered flushes; Support performed manual scale-up to restore service while fixes deploy.

Short-term fix: Deployed rate-limiter and circuit-breaker on ingestion path for telemetry aggregator to prevent full buffer floods. PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4321

Medium-term actions: Improve autoscaler resilience by adding a secondary utilization signal from job-level queue lengths and per-gpu attach latency. Add tuning guide for customers running sidecars that emit high-volume telemetry.
Follow-ups: Postmortem to be authored; recommended customer change: revert telemetry v2.3.4 batch settings and apply staggered flush pattern.

next_steps: Finalize postmortem and share with customer by 2026-03-18.
Ship autoscaler telemetry redundancy (secondary signal) and validate in load tests by 2026-04-01.
Create public-facing KB article with recommended sidecar telemetry best-practices for dedicated pools.
Coordinate with CS to review customer telemetry agent release (v2.3.4) compatibility checklist before future rollouts.
Monitor dedicated-pool NVLink alerts for 7 days and report anomalies weekly.
